cards.design_implication: If the research objective involves improving sodium-sulfur battery safety or cycle life, a design may conditionally include fluoroethylene carbonate as a co-solvent and a high-concentration sodium salt electrolyte system.
does_not_establish: Statistical significance of the interface formation.
Long-term degradation rates of the solid-electrolyte interface.
Causal mechanisms beyond the scope of the abstract summary.
cards.evidence_excerpt: the fluoroethylene carbonate solvent and high salt concentration not only dramatically reduce the solubility of sodium polysulfides, but also construct a robust solid-electrolyte interface on the sodium anode upon cycling
limitations: Support is limited to abstract-level claims.
Does not specify the exact salt concentration thresholds or formulation ratios.
cards.statement: Fluoroethylene carbonate solvent and high salt concentration reduce sodium polysulfide solubility and construct a robust solid-electrolyte interface on the sodium anode.

cards.design_implication: A design may conditionally incorporate indium triiodide as an additive if the goal is to address polysulfide corrosion and improve cathode reaction kinetics.
does_not_establish: Impact on battery capacity over specific cycle counts.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Indium triiodide as redox mediator simultaneously increases the kinetic transformation of sodium sulfide on the cathode and forms a passivating indium layer on the anode to prevent it from polysulfide corrosion
limitations: Support is limited to abstract-level claims.
Does not provide quantitative data on kinetic improvements or layer thickness.
cards.statement: Indium triiodide acts as a redox mediator to increase sodium sulfide transformation kinetics and forms a passivating indium layer on the anode.
